\title{Horizon-Gated Latent Prediction: Disentangling Persistent\\ Factors in Time Series}

\author{Jaechan Lee \\
University of Waterloo \\
Waterloo, Canada \\
\texttt{j2342lee@uwaterloo.ca}}

\newcommand{\fix}{\marginpar{FIX}}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
A single time series mixes factors that act on different timescales, which makes its embedding hard to interpret and to use. Methods that pull them apart have mostly keyed on the slow band of the signal, but a long-lasting factor need not be slow: it may ride on a nonlinear statistic such as an oscillation's frequency, where no low-pass reading reaches it. What the two kinds share is that both remain useful for predicting the distant future, while short-lived factors do not --- and that criterion is controlled by a variable prediction-based learning already contains, the horizon. We propose Horizon-Gated Latent Prediction (HGLP), which places a single soft threshold on that axis: beyond it the gate withholds a designated subspace, $\zmix$, from the predictor, so the only remaining route to lowering long-range error is to record the current state in the block that is left, $\zslow$; a cross-covariance penalty and a per-block LayerNorm hold the two apart. Because the horizon exists only while training, this is a criterion no post-hoc rotation of a frozen embedding can apply. We also propose a block-by-factor evaluation protocol and a single-number Separation Index (SEP), and show that the gate, the penalty and a latent prediction target are each necessary. On synthetic data built so that persistence and slowness disagree we lead label-free post-hoc rotation; on two real datasets (PTB-XL ECG, HAPT activities) the picture is mixed and Slow Feature Analysis mostly leads. We then audit our own claim: decomposing SEP shows the entire shortfall sits on the one term the objective cannot enforce, exclusion, and a non-linear probe applied equally to every method collapses that term and no other --- so the separation we demonstrate is a linear-level one. Finally, the coefficient governing that term can be chosen with no task labels at all, agreeing with the label-based choice in all six settings.
\end{abstract}
